newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower on Iraq impact.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower on Iraq impact.

text.p: Stocks closed lower after volatile trading on Thursday as fears of another "oil shock" dampened sentiment, which was recently buoyed by the expected expansion of foreign shareholding limit, brokers said.
The composite stock index closed 4.50 points lower at a provisional 787.14.
"Rising crude prices emerged as an additional burden to the already staggering economy," said Yoo Jae-kyong of Daishin Securities.
Brokers said the market would continue to fluctuate on Friday with investors taking a wait-and-see stance.

Brokers said high oil prices could deal a serious blow to South Korea, which relies mostly on the Middle East for crude imports. "Trade deficit will widen further and inflationary pressure will mount because of the Iraq crisis," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities. The United States launched missile attacks on Iraq this week.

Brokers said the central bank's announcement on August money supply figures and its plan to pump in five trillion won into the economy for the Korean Thanksgiving holidays had little impact. The bank said the M2 money supply grew 17.4 percent in August, compared with a 14.7 percent rise a year ago.
Brokers said the market was unlikely to fall drastically, because of counterbalancing factors such as the launching of savings scheme for stock investment in October.
The finance ministry will give tax breaks to workers investing in the bourse through savings accounts with securities houses. Brokers said this would attract about 1.5 trillion won.
Margin trading in the second tier stocks, which has been permitted from this month, was a boosting element.
The September futures contract ended down 1.8 points to 83.40, while the KOSPI 200 shed 0.88 point to 83.89.
